definition: The rule that refuses a hand-off of delegated work back up the line of hand-offs, to an agent that already handed the task down, so two agents cannot pass one task between them forever.
A grade for an enforcement mechanism, named by what an adversary would have to defeat to make the mechanism's claim false; there are five: Observed, Coordinated, Brokered, Confined and Attested.
The assurance mode in which the act may happen anywhere and the system keeps only best-effort evidence recorded afterwards, so there is nothing for an adversary to defeat.
The assurance mode in which cooperating clients declare their claims, roles, commitments and messages before acting, so an adversary need only decline to declare.
The assurance mode in which a chosen credential or effect channel passes through a broker the daemon owns, so an adversary must defeat that broker.
The assurance mode in which operating-system restrictions leave the process no other route to the protected effect, so an adversary must escape that confinement.
The assurance mode in which a key is released, or a result accepted, only to an environment whose measured build matches a published identity, so an adversary must subvert the measured environment.
The kernel component that checks operations already recorded in the log against the rules and reports or responds to violations; it detects and cannot always prevent.
Refusing a forbidden change before it takes effect, so that the forbidden state is never reached; contrasted with enforcement, which notices a violation afterwards and responds.
A component that checks every access to protected state, that other programs cannot alter, and that is small enough to verify (Anderson; Lampson).
A copy of a record that can be searched and displayed anywhere but carries no authority: writing to it changes nothing.
A number that increases every time a lock or lease is granted and is presented with every write, so the resource can refuse a holder whose lease has since passed to someone else.
A proposed fair lock in which each waiting agent leaves a numbered ticket in shared state and the agent releasing a claim hands it to the lowest ticket, with no background scheduler.
The signed record of who granted which permission to whom: a chain of grants, each allowing no more than the one before it, that a verifier can check signature by signature.
The record of which delegated task was handed down from which, used to detect a task being passed around in a loop.
A numeric signal an agent leaves in shared state for other agents to read, whose weight decays over time until it is deleted.
Hobbes's word, borrowed by this book, for the one authority whose rules every party accepts before acting; in a harbor, the daemon.
A piece of evidence the kernel can re-check by itself, such as a passing test identifier or a released claim, and the only thing that can close a commitment as done.
A step that passes through a point where the runtime can refuse it before it takes effect, such as a file write, network egress or a git push.
A step that completes before any point where the runtime could refuse it, such as the model emitting a token, reading its context or forming a plan.
The finite set of event types a system can emit; it is split into a controllable and an uncontrollable part.
The set of histories that are physically possible before any rule is imposed.
The program that, after each history, decides which controllable events to block next.

The property of a rule that no uncontrollable event, possible after an allowed history, can lead out of the rule; exactly the rules with this property can be enforced before the fact without losing allowed behavior.
The property of a rule that no two histories the runtime cannot tell apart call for different decisions about the same controllable event.
A proposed extension of the oracle vocabulary with delta oracles (a measured before/after improvement) and AST assertions (a structural property of the code), both re-checkable by the daemon.
A method that measures how safe a deployment stays when a capable model may be trying to defeat its safeguards, by having a red team supply the model's behavior.
